text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: service=hosted-inference-heartbeat incident=PD#88321 severity=high. Trigger: heartbeat failures spiked across multiple inference hosts (6 hosts). Paging policy: primary -> secondary -> manager.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty created incident PD#88321. Pages sent to primary oncall (alex). Secondary policy scheduled in 2m if no ack. Duplicate events observed, dedup key: heartbeat-service-1.

alex: ack'd via mobile. I'm pulling logs now. seeing repeated liveness failures at ~15s intervals.

maria: I got 4 pages in a row — phone blew up. can someone confirm if PD is deduping?

sre_lead: looking. Dashboard shows 6 parallel alert events from the same service; looks like a fanout from a mis-evaluated heartbeat metric. PD dedupe key changed due to host label flapping.

alex: here's the quick log tail:
```\n2026-03-15T04:12:03Z host-a inference LivenessProbe failed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T04:12:18Z host-b inference LivenessProbe failed: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T04:12:33Z host-c inference LivenessProbe failed: context deadline exceeded
```\n
maria: impact? are clients erroring?

sre_lead: yes — 5xx rate on hosted inference spiked to ~8% for ~12 minutes. Most requests are timing out while probes flap. Customer-facing latency increased.

ops_manager: Manager escalation warning will fire in ~60s if PD remains unacked. Heads-up to SREs — manager will be paged soon.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) silence repeated PD pages for this dedupe key, 2) mark incident as acknowledged, 3) remove bad hosts from LB, 4) bump liveness timeout and roll.

maria: I'm executing a quick silence.
```\n# silence via PagerDuty API (temporary)
curl -X POST "https://api.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD#88321/alerts"
 -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"status":"acknowledged"}'
```\n
pagerduty-bot: Silence applied to PD#88321 by maria. Secondary escalation suppressed. Manager escalation still queued (will fire if silence removed).

sre_lead: taking host-c and host-d out of the load pool: `kubectl cordon host-c && kubectl drain host-c --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then restart inference service with safer liveness: `HEALTH_TIMEOUT=30s`

alex: patched helm values and pushed a canary: increased liveness timeout + jitter to reduce synchronized flapping. Rolling to 10% then 100%.

maria: verifying telemetry — error rate trending down. 2% and falling.

ops_manager: manager escalation triggered (PD) during the fanout window but was auto-muted after silence. I responded to the page and confirmed we have mitigation in flight.

sre_lead: root cause hypothesis: liveness probes set too aggressively (5s) combined with a maintenance job that briefly increased CPU load across nodes -> synchronized probe failures -> metric labels flapped (host labels changed) -> PD dedupe key variation -> multiple alerts -> escalation fanout.

alex: quick checklist completed: muted PD duplicates, drained unhealthy hosts, rolled liveness change, scaled temporary capacity +1 pool. Rolling back is easy if we see regressions.

maria: writing a short incident note and linking to postmortem doc.

incidentbot: Incident PD#88321 resolved and closed by alex. Duration: ~20 minutes from first page to full restoration. Customer impact: ~8% error rate for ~12 minutes affecting hosted inference customers during spike; no data loss. Postmortem (draft): https://redwood.internal/pm/reports/PD-88321-thundering-heartbeat (will expand).

alex: thanks team. follow-up action items: 1) increase default liveness timeout in base chart, 2) add jitter/randomized probe offsets, 3) update alert dedupe to include stable service_id label, 4) add PD automatic suppression for known-heartbeat-fanout for 5m.

maria: agreed. I'll own the alert rule change and the PR.

sre_lead: i'll add the postmortem and link infra runbook changes.

ops_manager: good job triaging quickly. Closing thread — please add any missing notes to the postmortem. :thumbsup:
